source_batch.unit_label: BRBL Module B unit 4: Payment and Settlement Systems Act — Distinguish application, inquiry, authorisation conditions, refusal, revocation and statutory appeal

facts.statement: Courseware describes application/inquiry, approval factors, conditions and refusal hearing, six-month disposal endeavour, revocation and Central Government appeal.
facts.locator: S04 printed pp. 180–181; PDF page = printed page + 19

facts.statement: Sections 5–7 require application and permit inquiry, with specified authorisation considerations/conditions; refusal involves written reasons and hearing. Six months is a disposal endeavour, not deemed approval. Section 8 revocation has specified grounds and qualifications; section 9 permits the specified refusal/revocation appeal within 30 days of communication and endeavours disposal within three months.

payload.title: An application clock is not an operating licence
payload.core_explanation_md:
Applying under Section 5 starts a process. Section 6 permits RBI to enquire into the particulars, operating capacity and other relevant matters. Section 7 addresses authorisation using considerations such as design, security, settlement, management, financial status and consumer interests.

The resulting authorisation states its effective date and conditions and can include fees and security. The six-month language is an **endeavour to dispose of the application**, not a rule that silence grants a licence. A project plan should therefore separate submission, enquiry responses, grant, effective date and compliance with conditions.

self_check.prompt_text: Does expiry of the six-month disposal endeavour itself establish permission to operate?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. It is not a deemed-authorisation rule.

payload.title: Read the order and its route before advising on a challenge
payload.core_explanation_md:
Refusal under Section 7 involves written reasons and a reasonable opportunity of being heard. Section 8 addresses revocation, including specified grounds and qualifications; the normal hearing provision is not the entire section because it has an additional exception. An order can also need safeguards for affected persons.

Section 9 gives the specified applicant or provider an appeal to the **Central Government**, covering refusal under Section 7(3) as well as revocation under Section 8. Its text uses communication of the order as the appeal-period trigger. Record the order and receipt evidence, then obtain the appropriate legal review; this batch does not grade an exact filing date.

self_check.prompt_text: Is the Section 9 route limited to revocation alone?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. It also covers the specified refusal of an authorisation application.

payload.stem_md: Six months have elapsed after a complete application, but no authorisation has been issued. A project memo treats the statutory disposal endeavour as approval by silence. Which correction is needed?

options.text_md: The applicant may invent its own authorisation number
options.explanation_md: An internally generated identifier cannot substitute for RBI authorisation.

options.text_md: The Act contains no application process
options.explanation_md: Sections 5–7 address the application, inquiry and decision process.

options.text_md: A disposal endeavour does not itself create deemed authorisation
options.explanation_md: Operating permission must be established from the grant or an actual exemption, not elapsed time alone.

options.text_md: Only the company's auditor can issue the authorisation
options.explanation_md: The Act assigns the authorisation decision to RBI, not the company's auditor.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Operating permission must be established from the grant or an actual exemption, not elapsed time alone.

payload.stem_md: An applicant is refused authorisation under Section 7(3). A handbook says Section 9 provides a route only when an existing provider's authorisation is revoked. What should be restored?

options.text_md: The specified refusal as well as revocation can be appealed to the Central Government
options.explanation_md: Section 9 addresses both described types of order.

options.text_md: A customer's bank can cancel every RBI refusal itself
options.explanation_md: A bank does not acquire this power from the appeal provision.

options.text_md: Every refusal is automatically an authorisation on the following day
options.explanation_md: The statute does not create this automatic reversal.

options.text_md: Appeal always lies to the NI Act criminal trial court
options.explanation_md: That is not the statutory forum identified for this PSS authorisation appeal.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Section 9 addresses both described types of order.

payload.stem_md: An authorisation is issued with an effective date and specific operating conditions. What should a launch-readiness checklist verify?

options.text_md: Only whether the application fee was paid
options.explanation_md: Fee payment alone does not show that the grant is effective or that its conditions are satisfied.

options.text_md: The grant's effective date and compliance with the stated conditions
options.explanation_md: The authorisation carries operative terms that must be checked, not merely the fact that a document exists.

options.text_md: Whether a marketing announcement was posted
options.explanation_md: Marketing publicity cannot replace the effective date or conditions.

options.text_md: Whether a rival operator approved the project
options.explanation_md: A competitor's opinion is not the statutory grant or a condition imposed by RBI.

payload.correct_explanation_md: The authorisation carries operative terms that must be checked, not merely the fact that a document exists.
